sections.title: Core Thesis
paragraphs: The world moves at the speed and cost at which people and goods move. Make a dent in that, and you change how the world works.

Navier builds the vessels and operating infrastructure for high-speed, high-throughput, energy-efficient maritime transportation. Our vessels open new routes; distributed manufacturing scales the fleets; our strategic maritime nodes power and service them — and the network is open to compatible vessels from any manufacturer, all on one standard.

Navier earns recurring revenue on every journey, and every vessel and node added makes the network more valuable. One standardized platform compounding over passenger transport, cargo logistics and defense.

sections.headline: Three Costs Have Kept Maritime Stuck for Fifty Years
sections.subhead: A $1T industry moving ~90% of global trade on technology that hasn't fundamentally changed

cost.title: EXPENSIVE TO BUILD — NO SHARED PLATFORM
cost.body: Each new requirement restarts the design. Nothing compounds.

lever.title: CHEAP TO BUILD
lever.bridge: Same core in every hull — design cost amortizes across the line, and unit cost falls with every boat built.

cost.title: EXPENSIVE TO MOVE — THE SPEED PENALTY
cost.body: Water is 800× denser than air. Speed or cost: pick one.

lever.title: CHEAP TO MOVE
lever.proof: 7–13× lower energy cost per mile vs diesel
lever.bridge: Hydrofoils lift the hull out of the water — the drag behind the speed penalty is gone, and energy per mile drops 7–13× vs diesel.

cost.title: EXPENSIVE TO OPERATE — CREW-HEAVY BY DESIGN
cost.body: A full crew on every vessel, hands-on maintenance, low utilization.

lever.title: CHEAP TO OPERATE
lever.bridge: The software flies the boat — one operator oversees many vessels, so $50/hr per boat becomes ~$10/hr of fleet oversight.

why_now.title: Why now — the window is open.
why_now.body: Idle waterways · coastal security back on the agenda · U.S. shipbuilding constrained · diesel fleets aging out.

sections.closing_line: Speed & cost — no longer a trade-off.
